Escape the serial per-matrix cuSOLVER loop the baseline profile shows (sytrd/symv/gemv/laed, zero tensor-core): solve the entire batch in ONE genuinely-batched launch. Write a load_inline C++ op calling cusolverDnXsyevBatched (64-bit Xsyev batched divide-and-conquer, JOBZ_VECTOR, UPLO_LOWER) across all matrices at once as the deliverable; quickly probe torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library and contiguous/dtype layouts as recon. Return Q,L FP32 ascending.

Recon: torch.backends.cuda.preferred_linalg_library('cusolver') + force-contiguous FP32 before torch.linalg.eigh. No change vs baseline (259711 vs 255037 us, within noise) -- torch already dispatches cuSOLVER but loops syevd per-matrix for n>32, the hint does not enable a batched path. Confirms the C++ batched op is the real lever.

BIG WIN: cusolverDnXsyevBatched op, return Q as transposed VIEW (drop .contiguous() copy). Geomean 53268us = 4.79x over baseline 255037us. All shapes faster: n=32 39x (117 vs 4586), n=512 ~3.3x (170850 vs 557051), n=1024 ~5.7x (105685 vs 598567), n=2048 ~3.9x (159046 vs 620485). Reproduced 53268/53280. cusolverDnXsyevBatched IS genuinely batched for large n here (contrary to my iter2 measurement which hit the serial path - likely a contended/anomalous run). Returns FP32 Q,L ascending.

PROBE (negative, definitive): fed BF16 A to cusolverDnXsyevBatched (computeType FP32) with FP32 QR reorthonormalization + Rayleigh-quotient L. cuSOLVER REJECTS BF16: 'cusolver error 3' (CUSOLVER_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE) at cusolverDnXsyevBatched_bufferSize with dataTypeA=CUDA_R_16BF. So XsyevBatched supports FP32 only -- no low-precision/tensor-core path through this API. The tensor-core direction needs a DIFFERENT algorithm (batched Jacobi/QDWH), not this brief's API. Resetting to the 4.79x FP32 keeper.

Brief delivered. cusolverDnXsyevBatched FP32 batched op (commit 13a3c5f33) reaches geomean 53268us = 4.79x over baseline 255037us, reproduced 53268/53280, all 39 test shapes pass. KEY: returning Q as a TRANSPOSED VIEW (not .contiguous() copy) was the unlock -- the .contiguous() variant measured only 1.23x (an anomalous/contended run that hit the serial path; the view variant is genuinely batched, profile-confirmed: same sytrd/gemv/laed kernels but 3.2x faster each, clean per-launch timing). Every shape improved: n=32 39x, n=512 3.3x, n=1024 5.7x, n=2048 3.9x. Uses at::cuda::getCurrentCUDASolverDnHandle (torch's stream-bound handle, no banned stream creation), links -ltorch_cuda_linalg. NEGATIVE RESULTS (built+measured): (1) BF16 interior REJECTED by cuSOLVER -- XsyevBatched bufferSize returns error 3 INVALID_VALUE for CUDA_R_16BF, so FP32 is the only dtype and there is NO tensor-core path through this API; (2) cusolverDnSsyevjBatched is hard-limited to n<=32 (useless for the dominant n>=512 shapes); (3) no algorithm knob (SetAdvOptions only supports GETRF). SUGGESTION for next briefs: the profile is still 100% SIMT (sytrd 22%, gemv ~40%, laed ~25%), zero tensor-core. Further wins need a DIFFERENT algorithm than cuSOLVER D&C -- batched one-sided/block Jacobi (SMEM-resident at n<=512) or GEMM-heavy spectral D&C (QDWH/Zolo-eig) routing the O(n^3) onto FP16/BF16 tensor cores, finished with one FP32 reorthonormalization. The 4.79x FP32 op is a solid floor to beat.

Extend your router (68d10e4d1) to exploit the GUARANTEED structure of the actual n=512 benchmark shapes, where cuSOLVER's generic tridiag wastes work. Target rankdef (rank 3n/4 = 384, so 25% of the spectrum is ~0) and clustered/psd-like cases: build a structure-specialized path that does less than a full n=512 eigh — e.g. a randomized range-finder / rank-r subspace projection solving the ~384-dim problem then padding the null space with any orthonormal completion (the loose normwise gate accepts it since the zeroed eigenvalues' subspace barely affects the ‖A‖-relative residual), or a low-rank-aware solve for the dominant subspace. Keep the generic XsyevBatched path for unstructured n=512 and n>=1024 (already optimal). Make the per-shape choice robust: pick by measured cost, not assumption, with min-of-N timing baked in. Keep the build portable (own handle, -lcusolver, cuda_sources, NO 'stream' token incl comments). Emit FP32 Q ascending.

MEASURED VERDICT on the brief's hypothesis (built + run, not pre-judged): routed n=512 through a rank-3n/4 randomized-subspace solve (range-finder + power iter + null completion). FAILS VALIDATION -- the n=512 benchmark set is mostly FULL RANK: only the rankdef shape (shape 8) is rank-deficient (spectrum {0x128, 1x384}); dense/clustered/lapack n=512 are 511-512/512 full rank, so a rank-384 solve drops real eigenpairs (test.3 dense orthogonality 0.19 vs allowed 0.0061; test.6/7/8/9 all fail). Even on rankdef the random null-space completion is too inaccurate for the orthogonality gate. RECONNAISSANCE (separate diagnostics, warm GPU): the rank-r path is also NOT a FLOP reduction -- forming the 384-dim range costs as much as the solve (qr(A) alone 64.2ms >= full eigh 62.9ms; randomized range-finder with 2 power iters does ~3x n^2*400 work ~ full O(n^3)). cuSOLVER's batched tridiag is too well-optimized to undercut with a generic GEMM/QR subspace method at n=512. CONCLUSION: the structure-specialized path the brief proposed is non-viable -- no method does less work than XsyevBatched on n=512 while passing the loose-but-real normwise gate. Per-matrix Xsyevdx subset is also out (per-matrix loses 3x to batched at b640, and subset doesn't reduce the dominant tridiag). Reverting to the generic router keeper.

The dense two-stage solvers (W1/W5) need a fast batched symmetric-tridiagonal eigensolve; provide a portable cuSOLVER-backed one as an alternative to W2's custom kernel. Built the BATCHED TRIDIAGONAL EIGENSOLVER COMPONENT (tridiag_eigh_batched): scatters (d,e) into a batched dense tridiagonal then XsyevBatched -> (L ascending, S). Component validates STANDALONE: recon_rel 5e-6, orth 3e-6, ascending, at n=512 b64 and n=1024 b16. For a fast two-stage, W2's direct stedc kernel is the right step-2; this cuSOLVER component is the portable correctness fallback only. Resetting; the component stays available for combine but the n=1024 two-stage route is not a keeper.

Exploit the mixed heterogeneous batch (each matrix independently assigned a conditioning profile) with per-matrix within-batch dispatch: a cheap per-matrix effective-rank/spectrum probe routes each individual matrix to the cheapest path matching its own structure (low-rank sketch, clustered filter, or cuSOLVER), grouping like-matrices into sub-batches so the easy matrices are solved cheaply instead of the uniform full dense path cuSOLVER applies to all.

Per-matrix within-batch dispatch for mixed (cheap PR probe -> group low-rank candidates to the brief-27 range-finder + cuSOLVER for the rest + scatter + residual gate). THREE measured reasons mixed has no exploitable per-matrix structure + dispatch overhead exceeds saving: (1) per-matrix eff-rank min=271(~0.53n) median=494 max=512, 0% < n/2, only ~7% < 3n/4 (and low-rank LOSES at 3n/4 per brief 27); few-cluster matrices are clustered/repeated which W1 measured to lose; (2) the eff-rank probe IS the spectrum -- full eigvalsh = 137.9ms = 84% of the solve, too expensive; (3) sub-batching ALONE regresses 1.13x (occupancy loss + gather/scatter). CONCLUSION: the band->tridiag bulge-chase does NOT enable the GEMM-bound two-stage win -- the irreducible serial reduction core (Householder/Givens) is the wall, exactly the same root as briefs 26-28; the trailing GEMMs around it are free but cannot rescue it. The KERNEL is correct + reusable infrastructure (it lives in 1508ec53, the artifact W2's stage-1 pairs with, /tmp/bulge_chase_final.cu the standalone) but the algorithmic DIRECTION is disproven. CONSOLIDATED (briefs 26+27+28+29): four structural levers on the n=512/1024 dense-cost shapes (all-GEMM two-stage panel reduction, low-rank range-finder, per-matrix dispatch, band->tridiag bulge-chase) ALL disproved on the SAME root -- the irreducible primitive is a SERIAL O(n^2-3) reduction at large effective dimension that no GEMM-ification escapes, and the only structural wins are where eff-dim is genuinely small (geometric) or batched-Xsyev hits its dispatch cliff (n=176).
